record.paper_title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: Consider Monte Carlo M systems, meaning probabilistic morphogenetic systems that accept an instance if a distinguished floating object yes appears within polynomially many steps with probability at least 1/2 and reject if yes never appears. What is the exact computational complexity class of decision problems solvable by such systems in polynomial time in the semi-uniform sense? In particular, does this class include PSPACE?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 What is the exact characterization of the class of problems solvable in this way by Monte Carlo M systems in polynomial time? Does it, for instance, contain also the class PSPACE?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Morphogenetic systems (M systems) are a class of computational devices generalizing membrane (P) systems, in which "tiles" (geometric objects) and "floating objects" interact in a Euclidean space according to local probabilistic rules that allow tiles to attach, detach, and form structures, with floating objects diffusing among compartments.

A Monte Carlo M system is a probabilistic M system used as a decision device in the following way. Fix a distinguished floating object, denoted yes. For an input instance x of a decision problem, a family {Π_x} of M systems is constructed (the semi-uniform setting: a separate system Π_x is built for each instance x by a deterministic polynomial-time construction). The system Π_x is run for at most p(|x|) computation steps, where p is a fixed polynomial. The acceptance convention is:
  • If x is a yes-instance, then with probability at least 1/2 the object yes appears in a designated output region within p(|x|) steps.
  • If x is a no-instance, then the object yes never appears in the output region during the computation.

Let MCM-P denote the class of decision problems decidable in this semi-uniform Monte Carlo polynomial-time sense by M systems.

Question: Determine the exact characterization of MCM-P in terms of standard complexity classes. In particular, decide whether PSPACE ⊆ MCM-P.
artifact.status_search_result: No published characterization of the complexity class of polynomial-time semi-uniform Monte Carlo morphogenetic (M) systems was found. The problem is stated as an open problem in surveys on morphogenetic systems and no subsequent paper resolving it (in particular settling whether PSPACE is contained in this class) appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: overview and open problems (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on morphogenetic systems including the complexity characterization of Monte Carlo M systems.
status_evidence.claim: The exact complexity class of polynomial-time Monte Carlo M systems and its relation to PSPACE is posed as an open problem.
